subject.title: fix(sms): isolate validated webhook quotas per sender

question: Should validated SMS callbacks retain an aggregate account or route admission bound in addition to the proposed per-sender quota, or should the repository intentionally accept unlimited aggregate sender fan-out?
rationale: The proposed sender key removes the existing aggregate effect of the address-scoped dispatch budget; choosing the remaining availability and abuse boundary is product and security policy, not a mechanical repair choice.

options.title: Keep sender fairness with an aggregate bound
options.body: Add a documented account- or route-level accepted-work cap alongside the sender quota so one sender cannot cross-throttle peers while many valid senders cannot create unbounded aggregate ingress work.

options.title: Accept independent sender budgets
options.body: Merge the sender-only policy and explicitly document that signed traffic from many distinct senders may receive many independent 30/minute budgets.

options.title: Pause for SMS ingress policy
options.body: Defer this behavior change until an owner defines the supported overload and upstream-retry contract for validated Twilio callbacks.

recommendation.title: Keep sender fairness with an aggregate bound
recommendation.body: Add a documented account- or route-level accepted-work cap alongside the sender quota so one sender cannot cross-throttle peers while many valid senders cannot create unbounded aggregate ingress work.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest supplied context for the proposed Twilio sender-scope behavior and related SMS/RCS ingress work; an SMS-area owner should make the final policy call.
